answer: Unique-challenge answer registry. Each identity must answer a fresh randomly generated logical puzzle whose solution is a fable of arbitrary constants; the registry stores only a hash. Any new registration must submit an answer that does not collide with any stored hash, so an attacker fabricating N identities pays N separate solver-hours. A solved puzzle expires unless renewed, creating a residual relic of past effort that cannot be copied. Reusing one answer yields no nectar: the hash collision rejects the whole batch, so scaling requires linear unique work per identity.
